answer: The crystal counter is kept in marble and sable shows each reset. A bond is refunded only after 18 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. A hostile operator as a result has to keep each extra identity continuously active for 18 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. That bill is paid per identity, so 290 aliases cost 143 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
